results.title: Hariharan on music, the North-South connect and his AI dilemma | The Hindu
results.content: Legendary playback singer Hariharan sits down with The Hindu to celebrate a remarkable milestone: 50 years in the music industry. Spanning over 15,000 songs across 10 languages and 30 ghazal albums, Hariharan discusses his musical journey, his roots bridging Mumbai and Chennai, training under legendary masters, recording with Kishore Kumar, the record-breaking success of his Hanuman Chalisa rendition, and his profound concerns regarding the “AI dilemma” in modern music.

Lalit Modi becomes British citizen, adding a new twist to India’s extradition efforts
results.content: IPL founder Lalit Modi has announced that he is now a British citizen, a development that could add another layer of complexity to India’s long-standing efforts to bring him back to face legal proceedings. While British citizenship does not automatically protect an individual from extradition or legal action, it may affect the diplomatic and legal processes involved. Modi continues to face scrutiny over allegations linked to his tenure as IPL chairman, though he has consistently denied wrongdoing and rejected being labelled a fugitive.

results.title: PM Narendra Modi arrives in Philippines to attend ASEAN-India Summit
results.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday arrived in Manila, Philippines, to attend the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, scheduled for November 17. Ahead of his departure, PM Modi said in a statement, “Our relationship with ASEAN countries is at the heart of India’s Act East Policy and occupies a central place in our MAHASAGAR vision.”

results.title: Every Chhath, the same question returns: Why is the Yamuna still polluted?
results.content: Every year during Chhath Puja, images of devotees standing amid toxic foam bring the Yamuna’s pollution crisis back into focus. Despite decades of court interventions, government plans and cleanup projects, the river remains heavily polluted as it passes through Delhi. Experts say the key challenge is not just increasing river flow, but stopping untreated sewage and waste from entering the river in the first place.
